sources.title: Kuaishou Java interview source note containing student-score SQL tasks
Structured repository question for per-student total score
MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual 14.19.1 Aggregate Function Descriptions
MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual 14.19.3 MySQL Handling of GROUP BY
Student total-score deterministic SQL fixture validation

claims.text: The raw interview note states a table with student name, subject name and score, then separately asks for each student's name and total score; the candidate keeps exactly that one aggregation task and does not merge it with the adjacent max-score SQL question.
MySQL aggregate functions operate on sets of values and are commonly used with GROUP BY; SUM returns the sum and aggregate functions ignore NULL values unless documented otherwise.

Selecting student_name together with SUM(score) while grouping by student_name avoids relying on a nonaggregated column that is absent from the GROUP BY key; this is compatible with strict ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY-style semantics.
The exact SQL returns Alice=170, Bob=70, Carol=NULL and Dave=180 on an 8-row deterministic fixture, verifying grouping, SUM and NULL behavior for the documented contract.

findings: The candidate answers only the source's first SQL sub-question and keeps the adjacent Zhang-surname/max-score task separate.
The SQL has the correct result grain: one group and one output row per student_name under the source's minimal three-column schema.
The answer explicitly treats the table/column identifiers as examples because the source does not provide physical names.
NULL handling and strict grouping claims are grounded in current MySQL 8.4 documentation rather than generic template assertions.
The deterministic fixture verifies the exact SQL and includes an all-NULL group, which prevents silently assuming NULL means zero.
The candidate identifies same-name students as a source-model limitation and does not pretend names are universally unique.
No production experience is fabricated; required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
